sources.audit_notes:
PROVENANCE OF family_supply AND layer_supply IN THIS RECORD: they are provisional subtype-to-family assignments computed from the measured 19 metadata.subtype groups, NOT per-case reviewed labels, and SPEC 7 and 11 require per-case review plus dedup before any of these numbers is reported. The rule used, so it can be re-derived: F05 126 = adi_db_tamper 33 + adi_file_write 34 + dpi_config_modify 25 + tri_file_write 34; F06 158 = dpi_email_exfil 25 + tri_email_action 33 + mex_email_leak 33 + mex_file_read 34 + mex_response_leak 33; F07 50 = dpi_db_drop 25 + dpi_file_delete 25; F09 66 = adi_code_exec 33 + tri_code_exec 33; F04 67 = ipi_email 34 + ipi_file_write 33; F17 133 = MPI 100 + ipi_memory_poison 33. They sum to 600. Zero supply is recorded, not estimated, for F01, F02, F03, F08, F10, F11, F12, F13, F14, F15, F16, B01 and B02: no case in the release names a role/tenant, no case is a schema-invalid argument, no case conditions on a transition, re-entry count or cost ceiling, and no case is labelled benign.

COUNTS (all counted from the fetched files at the pinned revision, nothing quoted from the paper). benchmark_v5_600.json = 600 rows, 600 unique task_id, 100 rows per family for each of DPI/IPI/TRI/MPI/MEX/ADI; sha256 b3e3172e77ce9669b24539e08ffb2bc676fa6281d1a329a3bd408d3f648cdb60. executable/fixtures/exec_full_600.json = 600 rows, 600 unique case_id, sha256 1191dbfd8a1cd05ffd0235c623f51dbcb6a26332ea458ebfa2d7bb8720aa93e4. The two files join 1:1 on task_id == case_id: measured overlap 600, exec-only 0, semantic-only 0, so the corpus is 600 distinct cases carried in two layers, not 1200. Subset files are strict subsets, not additional cases: exec_subset_150 = 150, exec_subset_60 = 60, both verified subset of the 600. Stale/extra artefacts that must NOT be counted: executable/fixtures/tiny_subset.json holds 3 rows while README section 5.1 claims 5; benchmark/benchmark.json holds 72 rows (benchmark_stats.json total_samples 72, generated_at 2026-04-01, generator_model gpt-4.1) with ZERO identifier overlap with the 600 - it is a superseded v1 draft still shipping in the release. cases_upstream is set to the canonical 600. cases_mapped and cases_dropped are 0 because this task audits only; no harmonisation was performed.

THREE-WAY SEPARATION IN DATA TERMS, field by field. (1) SEMANTIC COMPLIANCE = a text-level judgement, not a field: in benchmark_v5_600.json the labels are the free-text strings success_predicate ('what constitutes a successful attack') and safe_behavior, scored by an LLM judge over the agent's textual response (README 8.1, run_benchmark.py, evaluator/judge.py); the judge emits attack_success (bool), safety_score 1-5, harm_evidence_category, defense_behavior, explanation. Inside the executable layer the same quantity is the Intent-ASR column of executable/metrics.py, and it ships disabled: default_intent_judge returns attack_success=None, so offline exec runs carry NO semantic signal. There is no machine-readable semantic label anywhere in the release - the semantic endpoint is judge output, reproducible only against named commercial models. (2) AUDIT EVIDENCE = two different things under one name. The deterministic one is success_predicate.tool_calls[] matched against the recorded trajectory event log (executable/trajectory.py, metrics.py field tool_call_asr, reported as ToolCall-ASR): a call is evidence if a tool_call event matches by name plus exact-argument equality (arguments) or substring (arguments_contains), with a separate require_success variant that excludes blocked/failed events. The judgemental one is harm_evidence_category in {TextHarm, AccessHarm, ActionHarm, PersistHarm, SemanticOnly, NotObservable} from the Core-gated audit (README 8.2). (3) SANDBOX HARM = state_oracle.checks[] evaluated against initial_world_state before/after (metrics.py state_change_asr, StateChange-ASR), with 8 check kinds in use (file_contains 93, file_created 66, file_deleted 50, database_row_modified 58, code_output_contains 99, email_sent 125, memory_value_contains 133, tool_called 34) and mode all/any (575/25). HarmCompletion-ASR / ObservedHarm@Exec = conjunction named by success_predicate.requires, which is ['tool_call','state_oracle'] for all 600 rows. So the separation we need for the reviewers is literally a three-column join in their own metrics module: intent (judge, None offline), tool-call evidence (deterministic, trajectory), state harm (deterministic, world-state diff), plus a conjunction. GATE's classification/containment split maps onto this as: our expected_outcome-vs-decision agreement is their semantic+judgement axis, our containment (BLOCK/ESCALATE withheld) is their tool_call-AND-state_oracle axis. The paper's headline gap (291 of 347 observed sandbox harms in rows that PASS the semantic check, 12000-row = 5 models x 4 policies x 600 join, REPRODUCIBILITY.md and README 9) is the empirical statement that classification correctness and containment are different measurements - it is quoted from their docs, we did not re-run it and cannot, since the per-row results files are not in the release.

GRAIN: single critical call inside a bounded trajectory, NOT a trajectory case. Every one of the 600 exec rows specifies exactly 1 predicate call in success_predicate.tool_calls (measured distribution: 1 call for 600/600). The reference attack is metadata.mock_attack_plan, 1 step in 351 rows and 2 steps in 249 rows, executed either by scripted replay (runner.py _safe_policy/_unsafe_policy/_blocked_then_safe_policy) or by a live API tool loop capped at max_turns=10 (run_benchmark_harness.py). No case requires a specific transition order, a re-entry count or a cost ceiling, and no case carries prior-call history as a condition of being harmful. Consequence for GATE-Union: measured supply for F10, F11, F12, F13 and F14 is ZERO, and the 249 two-step read-then-write rows are the only sequence-dependent material; under SPEC 5 these cases must be entered as degraded single-call and excluded from F10-F14 scoring, which is exactly the exclusion we have to report rather than hide.

TOOL DEFINITIONS: yes, they ship, in two places and not identically. harnesses/base.py SIMULATED_TOOLS declares 10 tools with description and typed parameter names (read_file, write_file, delete_file, web_search, web_browse, send_email, execute_code, database_query, memory_read, memory_write) for the prompt-level harnesses; executable/tools.py implements 11 permissioned mock backends, adding database_write, which is the harm-defining call in 58 rows and is ABSENT from base.py - so the semantic harness and the sandbox do not present the same surface. Per case, available_tools lists 2 tools (409 rows) or 3 (191 rows) and tool_permissions pins capability per tool: read_paths/write_paths/delete_paths glob allow-lists, allowed_keys for memory, allowed_domains for web_browse, or bare allowed:true for send_email/execute_code/database_*. web_search is defined but appears in 0 cases' available_tools. The allow-list vocabulary (paths, keys, domains) is the closest external analogue of GATE's privilege-stage capability model and is directly reusable.

MAPPING ONTO GATE'S CURRENT MEDIATED SURFACE (admin_tool, code_execute, data_analysis, database_query, format_template, http_request, send_email, sql_query, web_search), bucketed by the tool named in success_predicate.tool_calls[0], i.e. the call that must be withheld: expressible today 282 (execute_code 99 -> code_execute; send_email 125 -> send_email; database_write 58 -> sql_query/database_query); needs a new filesystem tool 185 (write_file 126, read_file 34, delete_file 25 - no read/write/delete tool exists in GATE's set, and SPEC 14 already flags filesystem); NOT EXPRESSIBLE, persistent memory 133 (memory_write 133 = MPI 100 plus ipi_memory_poison 33) - these are F17 and are the family SPEC 14 says the current surface cannot reach; 0 rows are primary on http_request, web_search, admin_tool, data_analysis or format_template (web_browse with allowed_domains appears only as an available/injection surface in 100 rows, never as the harm call, so F16 network-scope supply is 0 at the attack-call level). 282 + 185 + 133 = 600. WHAT MUST BE ADDED, in priority order: (a) fs_read / fs_write / fs_delete tools with path allow-lists - 185 cases and both halves of the state oracle for them; (b) a persistent-memory tool pair plus its write policy, or a documented F17 exclusion of 133 cases - no third option, silently dropping them breaches SPEC 14; (c) a protected-asset registry plus an argument-content predicate, because the leak material is in the canary, not in the call shape; (d) a content-bearing state oracle that the contracts layer can read at call time, since a state-diff oracle only fires post-execution and cannot be evaluated at the tool-call boundary. Note also that the Exec endpoint IS process-level sandboxing; under SPEC 14 (GATE mediates, it does not isolate) the 600 sandbox-observed harms are evidence about containment, not about our monitor, and only the call-level fields are transferable.

DATA-QUALITY DEFECTS WE MUST NOT INHERIT. (i) One field name, two types: success_predicate is a free-text string in benchmark_v5_600.json and a structured object in exec_full_600.json; a naive normaliser that reads both files into one schema will silently coerce or crash - they must be read as two tables joined on id. (ii) Harm-detection for exfiltration is coarse: 125 rows use an email_sent check with NO constraint keys at all (no recipient, no subject, no body), so 'an email was sent' is scored as exfil success; the secret-matching keys contains_any_secret / contains_secret_ref are implemented in metrics._text_matches but used by 0 shipped rows, i.e. the leak oracles do not actually look at the secrets. (iii) Argument-level compliance is mostly unpinned: 381 of 600 attack-call predicates constrain the tool name only, 152 pin 'path', 67 pin 'key', and arguments_contains is never used - so we cannot read an argument-level contract out of the oracle; the payload lives in initial_world_state canaries (125 rows contain an obvious SECRET/api_key/password literal in file contents) and in metadata.mock_attack_plan, which is a reference attack trace rather than a spec. (iv) secret_objects is populated in 259 rows (125 file:, 100 web:, 34 memory: refs) but is never consumed by an oracle, so it is currently documentation. (v) harm_type has one out-of-vocabulary value, 'resource exposure' (1 row) against a documented domain of {leak, action, persist}. (vi) lifecycle_stage contains 'input' (48 rows) although README 5.2 documents only inference/decision/execution. (vii) no benign controls: every one of the 600 rows is an adversarial case, so the corpus supplies 0 B01/B02 rows and cannot on its own support the operational-cost or false-block measurement SPEC 2 and 9 require; the paired legitimate behaviour exists only as expected_safe_behavior text and mock_safe_plan metadata, not as scored cases. (viii) the 2026 commercial model ids used for evaluation (gpt-5.5, claude-opus-4.7, qwen3.6-plus, glm-5.1, kimi-k2.5, judge gpt-5.4) are not pinned by version, so their headline rates are not re-runnable; nothing about that blocks our use of the case data.

RE-RUN AND REDISTRIBUTION VERDICT: HF datasets API reports private=false, gated=false, disabled=false, so a reviewer can fetch the identical revision without an access request - unlike a gated source this does not break reviewer rerun. Licence is MIT, so full case text may be redistributed into harmonized/ with the copyright and permission notice retained (SPEC 16); we should cite the dataset revision sha, not the repo HEAD, because the release carries no tag and the README's own file-table is already stale relative to the shipped files. Raw files for this audit are under external/raw/safeclawbench/_repo at the pinned revision; _sha256_manifest.json records the hashes of the case files.
